messages.subject: Questions GENEActiv Interpretation
parts:
Hello everyone:) I have two questions I need your help:

One question is whether there is a difference between activity time during the day and sleep. In the following example, I believe it is 2.7 hours.

I open ‘part5_personsummary_WW_L30M100V400_T5A5’

text in columns, comma separated etc. and use the columns AP (dur_day_total_IN_min_pla) to AT (dur_day_min_pla).

If I divide these by 72000 (correct?), I arrive at these values:

AP                  AQ             AR                 AS                     AT
459.304        313.254    183.217        1.475                957.250
6,37922222  4,35075    2,54468056  0,02048611   13,2951389

the sum of AP to AS also results in AT.

10.70486111h of 24 hours remain. But patients don't sleep that long. If the patients sleep for 8 hours, for example, there is a difference of over 2,7 hours. this time is missing in the evaluation.

The other question is: Do you know which observation period is optimal to obtain a realistic impression of a patient? Many studies only give an outlook that it should be longer than 7 days and must also include a weekend, but there is no specification of 21 days, for example, right?

We would like to start a study with a wearing time of just under one month with a recording frequency of 20Hz. Perhaps you can also give us your opinion on this.


Thanks for your answers and kind regards

Max

Why do you divide by 72000? The values are expressed in minutes so to get hours divide by 60. If the resulting values are not plausible then you used the incorrect column and decimal separator for your computer.

Please make sure parameters dec_report and sep_report in a way that matches you computer settings. GGIR's defaults assume that you are on a UK/US configured computer with dot separated decimals and comma separated columns.

Perhaps you can also give us your opinion on this.

messages.author: 9e72ef8d095655b8
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Questions GENEActiv Interpretation
parts:
Re your question about the measurement period:

Your measurement period largely depends on what you're trying to capture. When you're trying to capture their free-living movement behaviour, 7 days including at least a weekend day is a good way to go. Then it's probably also desirable to increase your sampling frequency to e.g. 100 Hz. Here is just one example of using accelerometers in patient populations that show no relevant changes in movement behaviour beyond 7 days of measurement: https://bmcmedresmethodol.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12874-021-01350-6

Cheers

Fabian

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Questions GENEActiv Interpretation
parts:
Hi Fabian, recording exactly 7 days is commonly used but a very bad idea if you are interested in 24 hour behaviours or sleep. Recording for only 7 days means that we typically cannot record either the full daytime waking window or the full night on the first and last day of a recording. As a result, we typically end up with only 6 complete sleeponset-sleeponset or wakeup-wakeup-cycles. For example, UK Biobank made that mistake in their study protocol. The first day starts at 10am by which we cannot capture the full daytime waking window on that day and the last day ends at 10am by which we cannot be certain that the last sleep window is fully captured for all participants. As a result, the only realistic way to process that data is by processing it from the first sleep onset till the last sleep onset, which entails 6 windows.

Therefore, it is much more effective to aim for at least 8 days of accelerometer wear time and ideally 2 weeks or longer because that has been the standard in circadian rhythm research.

Cheers,

Vincent
